subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB369 LANDED. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "the qualifying declarative in the source element that contains the statement that caused the condition to exist" -> OK, GR 4 a); cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "a qualifying declarative with the GLOBAL attribute in the next inclusive directly containing source element" -> OK, GR 4 b)). BOTH FORMATS ARE NOW IMPLEMENTED AND WITNESSED BY SPEC-DERIVED GOLDENS. FORMAT 1: __IoCheck's local tier (GR4 a)), then __outer.__RunGlobalUse walking outward over Format-1 GLOBAL declaratives only (ChainHasGlobalUse no longer counts a Format-2 GLOBAL declarative); conformance:cases/13.18.27-GLOBAL/pb369_global_file_use_selection is the spec-pinned witness for BOTH halves - a contained program's own USE on the inherited GLOBAL file beats the container's GLOBAL one (a), a declarative-free grandchild reaches the outermost GLOBAL one past a non-GLOBAL middle one (b). FORMAT 2: the selection is per STATEMENT, so there is no per-group engine hook any more; each unit that can see a report and whose GR4 chain (itself: any declarative; each container up to the declaring program: GLOBAL only) names one of its groups emits __BeforeReporting_{uid}(gi, globalOnly), and GENERATE / TERMINATE pass it to the engine, which asks it by ReportGroup.Index just before producing each group. The upstream blocker is gone: RD GLOBAL (13.18.27.3 SR1 e)) is implemented - the report-name, its groups and its sum counters are visible in contained programs (13.18.27.4 GR1/GR2) and reached through the __outer chain. conformance:cases/13.18.27-GLOBAL/pb369_global_report_use_selection witnesses a) (a contained program's own non-GLOBAL declarative beats the container's GLOBAL one; the container's own GENERATE runs its own non-GLOBAL one), b) past a non-GLOBAL middle declarative, the NEGATIVE of b) (a container's non-GLOBAL declarative is NOT selected for a contained GENERATE), and a CF FINAL group produced by a grandchild's TERMINATE. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985/2002/2014/2023 (the rule is headed FORMATS 1 AND 2; both formats, nested programs and the GLOBAL clause are COBOL-85).
